messages:
Tina: hit a strange one in canary: shared-slab + rapid tenant churn -> tenant X served stale prefixes after we accepted handback tokens from tenant Y. repro attached.
Omar: rough sketch of repro?
Tina: create tenants X,Y on same slab, make Y hot, then evict-window contraction moves tokens into X via handback. X then served reads referencing gen from Y for ~20s. logs: 
```
2026-03-01T11:02:01Z INFO handback: from=Y to=X tokens=3 owner_gen=42 owner_tenant=Y
2026-03-01T11:02:05Z ERROR readpath: tenant=X stale-prefix key=0x9a gen=42
```
Zoe: we treat handbacks as pure credits today. clearly unsafe across tenants unless we validate owner_gen against a local safe_gen.
Ben: agree. two options: (1) quarantine inbound cross-tenant handbacks for a short TTL, (2) tag handback with owner_gen and reject unless owner_gen <= lease.safe_gen(owner_tenant). reject -> force cold-prefill.
Omar: prefer (2) with a small_fastpath for tiny token counts to avoid churn. also emit metric handback.rejected{reason=gen_mismatch,src,dst}.
Tina: also need cursor safety: cursors must carry expected_prefix_gen and verify on resume. if mismatch return INVALID_CURSOR.
Zoe: tests: quick chaos test flipping ownership + assert readpath.stale==0, and microbenchmark for cold-prefill regression.
Ben: implementation estimate: tag + accept logic ~1 day, lease safe_gen plumbing + tests ~4 days.
Tina: ok action items: Ben implement owner_gen tagging; Omar wire lease safe_gen to receiver; Zoe add cursor-gen checks and tests; Tina add alerts/dashboards and canary config to disable shared-slab if needed.
deploy-bot: note: created issue INF-9933 (cross-tenant handback validation) assigned to Ben, Omar.
